newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was steady to weak on moderate to fairly good demand and moderate to heavy offerings.

Retail interest was for immediate needs for first of the month featuring, while forward interest was rather light. Processors were forced to control inventories on round cuts early in the period resulting in good demand at lower prices.
By week's end processors were able to better position themselves on these cuts enabling them to recapture most of their earlier losses.
Chuck cuts struggled all week to maintain steady levels and ended the trading period on a weak undertone as inventories became rather burdensome.

Rib cuts also struggled with the Select under the most downward pressure. Loin cuts traded uneven as Select product was steady to firm, while Choice product traded at weaker levels as these cuts were more abundant.

After weeks of discounting, Choice tenderloins are trading at the same levels as their Select counterparts. Closely trimmed items were generally steady on fairly good demand as these cuts were seen as good values.
Beef trimmings traded higher on moderate demand and light to moderate offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings.

For the week Select and Choice rib primal steady to $1.50 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal steady to $1.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal generally steady; Select loin primal $1.00 higher, Choice loin primal $1.00 lower; Closely trimmed items generally steady; Beef trimmings $3.50 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses dn .89 at $96.23; 700/850 dn .22 at $95.44; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses dn .47 at $92.78; 700/850 dn .09 at $91.86.
